Last-observer removal chooses cancelRetry when signal is unconsumed and fetch is active; retryer.cancelRetry only sets retry cancellation flag. Probe retains seed/fetching before late completion.
Last-observer removal chooses retryer.cancel({revert:true}); onCancel restores #revertState with idle and aborts controller. Probe observes seed/idle/aborted=true.
Retryer resolve ignores settlement after status becomes rejected; Query success path only updates after retryer fulfillment. Actual late remote result updates only the unconsumed branch.
Official matrix records one queryFn call for each branch and both final success/idle states; state branch explicitly excludes paused pending behavior.

assertion_discrimination: Signal consumption varies independently of listener/transport cancellation; pre-resolution state and late resolution distinguish cancelRetry from cancel/revert.

required_claims.reason: cancelQueries creates options with revert:true default and returns Promise.all(...).then(noop).catch(noop), supporting its own rejection swallowing separately from fetch return semantics.
QueryClient.setQueryData calls setData(manual:true); success reducer resets fetchStatus only for nonmanual updates. Probe records all before-cancel states as fetching.
Manual success assigns #revertState=newState, and onCancel spreads that checkpoint then forces idle. Initial checkpoint is set at query.ts714-715; actual none/manual cases yield seed/edited.
setState dispatch only merges partial state; unlike manual success it does not assign #revertState. Source and raw-state probe show edited visible before cancellation but seed afterwards.
CancelledError with revert returns current data when defined; late retryer resolution is ignored after rejection. Actual original promises resolve seed/edited/seed and states remain success/idle.

assertion_discrimination: Three controls distinguish normal cancellation, public manual-success edits and raw state merges; both public promise value and late state are checked.

required_claims.reason: Observer.setOptions immediately defaults options and forwards to current Query even without listeners. Probe directly records cachedRetry=false before rejecting first request.
Query.fetch live retryer branch returns at608, preceding supplied options application at612-615. Probe never records duplicate call and subsequent fresh request still invokes newFn.
createRetryer captures context.options.retry and retryDelay; error handler consults captured config. Old callback executes once and first failure retries despite updated Query retry=false.
fetchFn resolves ensureQueryFn(this.options) on each invocation; retryer calls config.fn on each run. Probe records old,new and both pending callers resolve new-result.

New fetch creates retryer from current options; retryer calculates delay before shouldRetry/reject. Probe records freshError=new-failure, calls old,new,new and exactly one evaluation of each delay callback.
